description:
Permissions for a Nib window on a desktop. Only what the window actually calls: core:default for the window's own read-only queries and the event channel, the window commands the title bar, the close handler, Always on top and presenting use, where the window is and how big it is, which `nib screenshot` reads so it can say which rectangle to photograph, the two dialogs (open and save), the opener for links, for an export shown where it was saved and for the app's own folders, restart for an update installed by hand, the scheme chosen in the app said to a Mac's window, whose sheets and menus follow it rather than the page (see paintWindow in src/lib/theme.svelte.ts), and the two updater steps the plugin performs. The look for a new version is not one of them: which stream an install follows decides which endpoint it looks at, and only the builder in Rust takes endpoints, so the look is this app’s own `check_update` command and needs no permission. See src-tauri/src/updates.rs. The three presenting ones are for the window a presenter reads their notes in: it is created from JavaScript rather than from Rust, and where the screens are decides which of them it opens on. That window itself needs no permissions - it draws what the deck sends it over a broadcast channel and calls nothing. Notes are read and written by this app's own commands, so the fs plugin is not here and not built in. Nothing that gives the keyboard or the front, although the page does both: a site’s question under a web tab’s bar takes the keyboard back, because the page that asked was holding it and a page out of sight keeps it (see WebAsk.svelte), a Mac’s menu bar does too when a row of the window's is chosen while a web tab has it, and presenting brings the presenter's window forward when it is open already. Each asks the crate (`take_keyboard` and `raise_window` in src-tauri/src/placement.rs), which does neither in a run whose windows were sent off the screen, where either would put a window nobody can see in front of whoever is working. The phone builds have none of these plugins compiled in; see mobile.json.

Two labels, because New window opens a second one: `main` is the window the app starts with, and `nib-2`, `nib-3` and so on are what launch::new_window hands out. A webview whose label matches no capability is granted nothing at all, so it would come up unable to listen for an event, drag its own title bar or close itself. The presenter's window is `nib-presenter`, which the digits do not match, and it is meant to have nothing.

Webviews and not windows, which matters now that a web tab puts a second webview inside the window: a capability naming a window grants every webview in it whatever its own label says, and a website in a tab would then be holding the app's own permissions. Naming the webviews grants the app's own and nothing beside them - the webview a WebviewWindow builds carries the window's label, so these two patterns are the same two windows they have always been, and a web tab's `web-...` is not among them. A remote origin matches no capability here either, which is the other half of the answer; see src/web_tabs.rs.

The terminal's commands are the app's own and need no permission here, so they hold themselves to the same two labels: `pty_spawn` and the rest answer only the page of a document window, a session belongs to the window that started it and no other may type into, size, read or end it, and a shell is started by an id the crate found, never by a program the page names. See src/terminal.rs and docs/terminal.md.
